title: Xanthe and the Thorn
premise: Edmund Thornbury, a memory-thief who keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, has spent years making herself forgettable to survive. When a dying stranger presses a map into her hands and names her heir, Edmund learns she was born in Vellamere, a country erased from every record—including her own mind, by her own hand. Hunted by the guildmaster who raised her and shadowed by Xanthe, a knight sworn to erase what remains of Vellamere, Edmund must recover the memories she sold to find the door out of a country that no longer exists. In the end, Edmund reclaims her past at the cost of her invisibility, chooses love over duty alongside Xanthe, and opens the door—letting Vellamere finally die so its people can live.
about_author: I. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing documents belonging to nations that no longer exist. They write fantasy about memory, borders, and the things we trade away to stay safe, from a house full of unlabeled maps.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Thefts
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. She catalogs stolen memories for the Guild of Impossible Things, including one of her own she refuses to reread. A routine night establishes her rule: be forgotten, stay alive. Emotional beat: the loneliness of chosen erasure, and the first crack in it when a ledger entry about herself appears that she never wrote.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Drowned Bell
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A dying woman finds Edmund in a dockside tavern, presses a bloodstained map into her hands, and says 'Vellamere remembers you.' She dies before explaining. Emotional beat: terror—the map hums with memories Edmund recognizes as her own, sold long ago.

chapters.title: What the Guild Owns
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. She brings the map to guildmaster Corvane, expecting payment; instead he goes pale and demands it, revealing the guild trades in impossible things—and erased countries are the most profitable. Emotional beat: betrayal; the man who raised her looks at her like property.

chapters.title: Xanthe
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A knight of the Order of the Blank Page arrives to retrieve the map, bound by oath to unmake Vellamere's last traces. Watching Edmund, Xanthe hesitates for the first time in twelve years. Emotional beat: duty strained by an unexpected recognition—Edmund's face matches a portrait in a forbidden archive.

chapters.title: Running on Borrowed Streets
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Refusing to surrender the map, Edmund flees through the city using stolen escape-memories of streets she's never walked. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into dread as the borrowed memories begin bleeding into her own identity.

chapters.title: The Price List
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Hiding in a memory-broker's cellar, Edmund reads the guild's ledger of her own sales: childhood, a name, a face, a door. Each entry lists a buyer. Emotional beat: grief—the discovery that she chose this poverty of self, and the question of why.

chapters.title: An Uneasy Truce
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Xanthe corners Edmund but cannot strike; the map shows itself only to Vellamere's heir. They agree to travel together—each planning to betray the other. Emotional beat: wary, electric mistrust laced with reluctant fascination.

chapters.title: The Broker of Sorrows
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. To buy back her name-memory, Edmund must steal a grief from a grieving mother—a theft that leaves the woman hollow. Emotional beat: horror at her own trade; the price of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: Name Recovered
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Drinking back her name-memory, Edmund recovers her true name—Sable Vane—and fragments of a burning city and a mother's voice singing. Emotional beat: vertigo of becoming two people at once; Xanthe watches her grieve a home she can't remember.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The guildmaster catches up via a bought informant and offers Edmund everything: wealth, protection, permanent forgetting. He reveals the guild helped erase Vellamere—for a king who feared its door. Emotional beat: cold paternalism masking fear; Corvane needs her more than he admits.

chapters.title: The Order of the Blank Page
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Flashback chapter: how Xanthe was orphaned by Vellamere's fall and trained to erase it, believing the country was a plague of dangerous memory. Emotional beat: sympathy built for the antagonist-in-waiting; Xanthe's faith begins to itch.

chapters.title: Border of Fog
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Following the map, they reach a valley where fog swallows roads and the fog whispers in Sable's mother's voice. Xanthe saves Edmund from walking into it. Emotional beat: first real trust—an act of protection with no strategic value.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. They find survivors of Vellamere living unremembered in a fold between places, sustained by pooled memories. An old woman recognizes Sable. Emotional beat: belonging offered for the first time—and the terrible cost of keeping it.

chapters.title: What Erasure Costs
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The villagers show Xanthe the truth: the Order's erasures don't destroy countries, they strand their people outside existence. Xanthe's whole life reframes as complicity. Emotional beat: shattering of faith; the beginning of love against duty.

chapters.title: Corvane Descends
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Corvane and the Order assault the hidden village, buying the villagers' pooled memories to locate the door. The village burns out of existence. Emotional beat: rage and loss; Edmund realizes Corvane wants the door not closed but owned.

chapters.title: Ledger of Betrayals
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Captured and brought before Corvane, Edmund uses her knowledge of his own sold memories—she kept his ledgers—to blackmail him: she knows what he paid to forget. Emotional beat: reversal of power; the clerk becomes the threat.

chapters.title: The Door Beneath the Map
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Escaping with Xanthe's help, Edmund deciphers the map: the door out of Vellamere is made of returned memories—it opens only if every stolen piece comes home. Emotional beat: resolve; she must reclaim even the memories she'd rather keep buried.

chapters.title: Everything I Sold
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund drinks back her final memories: she erased Vellamere herself as a child, coerced by Corvane, to save her mother—and it failed anyway. Emotional beat: devastating self-knowledge; forgiveness of the child she was.

chapters.title: The Standing Stone
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the door, Corvane offers Xanthe restoration of her erased family in exchange for killing Edmund. Xanthe refuses—love against duty, chosen openly. They fight together. Emotional beat: the book's thematic heart stated in action.

chapters.title: Opening the Door
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund pours her recovered memories into the door and it opens onto Vellamere as it was—one breath of the country that no longer exists. Corvane, grasping for it, is pulled into the memory and unmade by everything he sold. Emotional beat: awe and terrible beauty.

chapters.title: Letting the Country Die
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. To free the stranded villagers, Edmund must let the door close forever, releasing Vellamere into death rather than preserving it as a prison. She does, mourning properly at last. Emotional beat: acceptance; survival redefined as carrying memory forward, not hoarding it.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Weeks later, Edmund and Xanthe rebuild among the freed villagers. Edmund keeps a new ledger—not of thefts, but of things remembered and returned. Emotional beat: quiet hope; the price of survival was everything, and it was worth paying together.
